text: The Kestrel planning summary for 3–10 November reflects later corrections, including archive max_workers of 26 and tenant queue_depth of 440. Client requirements set webhooks max_workers to 20 and timeout_s to 40, audit ttl_s to 510, and search queue_depth to 90. The rollout order is webhooks before alerts, shipping before checkout, indexer before notify, and session before ledger. Ownership is split among alpha (webhooks), beta (tenant), gamma (alerts and export, which shares a worker with alerts), and delta (auth). Hard rules prohibit an archive-to-media dependency, a shipping dependency on inventory, and any alerts-to-gateway path. One coupling example: an inventory ttl_s above 270 caps notify max_workers at 6. Undecided items include the linter, Rust rewrites, and a shared metrics library. The security review is due at month's end, and the budget review has moved to next Thursday.
